lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: The Experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: The August 2022–July 2024 role appears above the October 2024–May 2025 role, making the sequence harder to follow.

items.says: Education appears before the relevant professional experience.
items.because: Placing Education first delays the context that establishes the candidate’s direction.

items.says: The dashboard and on-call responsibility has no stated outcome.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the dashboards improved diagnostics or helped the on-call team.

items.says: The p95 latency result is buried after methods.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the reduction.

items.says: The shortened release cycle is buried after the actions.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the result.

items.says: The nightly-backlog result is buried after a long list of actions.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the operational outcome.

items.says: The word “which” has an unclear antecedent.
items.because: It does not clearly identify what removed the backlogs.

items.says: The onboarding and weekend on-call duties crowd the migration bullet.
items.because: They are separate duties that obscure the migration’s outcome.

items.says: The nightly-backlog outcome has no measure of its scale.
items.because: A reader cannot judge how often or how much the backlogs delayed dispatch.

items.says: The 68% backlog reduction has no stated baseline or endpoint count.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which before-and-after counts support the percentage.

items.says: The 40% latency reduction does not identify its comparison baseline.
items.because: Without the prior setup, readers cannot tell what changed or how to interpret the percentage.

items.says: The batching attribution is not established by the measured workload.
items.because: The line does not show that requests could coalesce or that batching reduced latency.

items.says: The 5% latency result is buried after a long method list.
items.because: A scanning reader may not reach the clearest statement of what changed.

items.says: “Using … reduced” leaves the subject unstated.
items.because: It is unclear who or what reduced latency.

items.says: The 5% latency reduction lacks a comparison setup and measurement context.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what configuration it was compared with or how latency was summarized.

items.says: One rollout per prompt cannot provide the within-prompt group-relative advantage used by standard GRPO.
items.because: With a group of one, the centered advantage is zero and its within-group variance is unavailable.

items.says: The sentence repeats that each update used one scored trajectory.
items.because: That restates the single-rollout choice without adding information.

items.says: The claim that training stabilized has no stated evidence.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what instability improved or how the change was assessed.

items.says: “AI-first engineering practices” does not say which practices were introduced.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what work the phrase refers to or what engineering skill it demonstrates.

items.says: The claimed downstream improvements are not specific enough to show what changed.
items.because: “Accelerating delivery and improving outcomes” gives no concrete result or comparison.

items.says: The stated 50% reduction is mathematically wrong; 900 ms to 600 ms is 33.3%.
items.because: The 300 ms decrease is one-third of the 900 ms baseline.

items.says: The stated 12% increase is wrong; 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points.
items.because: Relative to the original 71%, the increase is about 16.9%.

items.says: The metric categories give no example of the technical work involved.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what skill went into creating or integrating the metrics.

items.says: The Kendall correlation does not identify the two quantities being correlated.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the coefficient says about the evaluator’s performance.
